statement: A delivery van can safely carry at most $1{,}800$ pounds of driver and cargo combined. The driver weighs $180$ pounds, and each box to be loaded weighs $35$ pounds. What is the greatest number of boxes the van can safely carry on one trip with the driver?

choices.misconception: I found that $(1{,}800 - 180) \div 35 \approx 46.3$ and rounded up to 47, but 47 boxes would put the van over the limit.
I forgot about the driver and worked out $1{,}800 \div 35 \approx 51.4$, so I got 51 boxes.
I added the driver's weight to the limit instead of subtracting it, so I got $1{,}980 \div 35 \approx 56.6$ and 56 boxes.

hints: Write an inequality: driver plus boxes must be no more than $1{,}800$ pounds.
With $n$ boxes, $180 + 35n \le 1{,}800$. Solve for $n$, then remember that $n$ must be a whole number.
$35n \le 1{,}620$, so $n \le 46.28\ldots$ The number of boxes must be a whole number that does not break the limit.

solutions.reliable: With $n$ boxes the total weight is $180 + 35n$, which must satisfy $180 + 35n \le 1{,}800$. So $35n \le 1{,}620$ and $n \le 46.28\ldots$ The greatest whole number is $46$. Check: $180 + 35(46) = 1{,}790 \le 1{,}800$, but $180 + 35(47) = 1{,}825 > 1{,}800$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
